The context

When the gate queue
becomes the problem.

Manual guard logs and paper sign-in sheets make arrival time slower and harder to trust. This project provides a clear, traceable alternative for the SKSU Isulan main gate.

⌛

Peak-hour bottlenecks

Paper entries slow down arrival and departure during busy periods.

✎

Human error

Handwritten details can be incomplete, inconsistent, or difficult to read.

⌕

Hard retrieval

Finding a past record requires searching through physical log sheets.

◌

No instant view

Parents and authorities do not have immediate visibility at the point of logging.

The proposed response

Simple at the gate.
Deliberate by design.

A passive RFID student ID initiates an entry or exit event. The system confirms it visually, announces the status, and records the timestamp.

Research objectives

A system that makes every gate event accountable.

General objective

To develop an RFID-based student entry and exit monitoring system with voice notification and digital display.

Design and construct the system using a microcontroller, RFID reader, voice module, and monitor.

Read RFID tags, record real-time entry and exit timestamps, and manage student profiles.

Show verification details on the monitor and play voice announcements for each event.

Assess scanning speed, tag detection accuracy, reliability of logging, display and voice output, user acceptability, and operational efficiency.

System features

Feedback that keeps
the gate moving.

⌁

Contactless scanning

Passive RFID cards are read at the point of entry or exit.

◷

Real-time logging

Each valid event records an entry or exit timestamp.

▤

On-screen verification

Monitor feedback makes the event status immediately visible.

)))

Voice prompts

Pre-set English phrases announce the system status.

▦

Structured local database

Student profiles and records are retained on the local system.

↗

Admin reports

Structured records support future administrative reporting.

Scope & limitations

Focused for a
real gate setting.

01

Passive cards only. The system is designed for passive RFID cards; it does not support long-range or active tags.

02

Campus gate setting. The intended deployment context is the SKSU Isulan main gate.

03

Fixed English prompts. “Entry Recorded,” “Exit Recorded,” and “Access Denied” are pre-set; dynamic name pronunciation and multilingual output are outside scope.

04

Local data workflow. The design uses a local database with local server synchronization.

Who benefits

A better gate
experience for all.

The system is designed around clearer information, smoother entry, and a more reliable institutional record.

01

Administration

Structured event records can support more informed oversight of gate activity and future reporting needs.

02

Security personnel

Visual and voice feedback can reduce reliance on handwritten logs and simplify routine gate confirmation.

03

Students

A quick RFID tap offers a clear, contactless way to confirm entry or exit at the campus gate.

04

Visitors

A more orderly gate process can help make campus arrivals easier to understand and navigate.

05

Faculty & staff

Clearer gate activity records can support campus operations and institutional coordination.

Technology stack

Built from focused,
connected parts.

The proposed system connects physical identification, edge processing, visual feedback, voice response, and local record keeping.

Research methodology & evaluation

A practical path
to assessment.

  1. 01

    Design

    Define the gate flow, components, and required feedback.

  2. 02

    Build

    Construct the integrated hardware and software system.

  3. 03

    Test

    Observe transactions and component output in the campus setting.

  4. 04

    Evaluate

    Assess performance, reliability, and user acceptability.

Evaluation criteria

Scanning speed · Tag detection accuracy · Logging reliability · Display and voice output · User acceptability
